brief: brief-js177-design.md: four decisions before JS-177's Spec, from its design review. (1) The learned figure is price times speed over 1.2, in which D-046's share of 0.78 of the price is 0.65; a literal 0.78 refuses the throttled pair JS-161 admits (2.27 each against 2.5). (2) A figure lowered by a burst: recover by time with backoff, only on evidence, only at restart, or by the operator. (3) Whether the figure survives a restart: Postgres by hardware class with a 24 h expiry, not at all, or per pod or node; about 40 s to converge on a start that overstates (design, not measured). (4) What learning cannot see: the worker's own extractions beside a transcode, and contention the kernel does not show; state as limits, count extraction CPU, or measure first.
tradeoff: Given up by a pair of declared workers with 2.08 to 2.5 reference cores free each, and their viewers: a 3.2 job is admitted shared where it was refused, on figures that may have been computed without the 1.2 margin, until the learned figure corrects it. Given up by viewers of a lone worker slow for good: a film admitted that plays under real time in place of a refusal with its reason, at gaps that at least double up to a day or more, until the operator sets the optional ceiling. Given up until JS-178 merges: an undeclared worker relearns at every start. Given up on any host: a worker's own extraction beside a transcode is not told apart from slow hardware.
entry: (1) Option A: capacity is the price a worker keeps at 1.2 times real time; the shared rule keeps its measured meaning (each of two workers makes the job at 0.78 of real time alone) and reads 0.65 of the price free, for learned and declared workers; no price changes; DOMAINS.md invariant 58 and the docs change citing this. (2) Option A, bounded: a figure rises first from evidence, with no stall (any job that shows more, a shared play's own included), and by time only when no job has tested it; a timed rise the next job shows wrong at least doubles the gap to the next, with no cap under 24 hours, and the log names transcodeCores as the optional ceiling from the second. The brief's 'one stalled play an hour, only if a viewer asks then' is not accepted as stated. (3) Option A as JS-178, ahead of JS-056 and behind the household set: the figure is kept by hardware class while a worker of the class has run in 30 days (the 24 h expiry is rejected), as a start only; JS-178 also takes JS-177's criterion 5. The dogfood's declared figures stay as ceilings until then unless the owner chooses otherwise. (4) Option A: the limits are stated in docs/running.md and a worker that cannot read the kernel's figures says so; option B is BL-262; one row joins the pre-Spec spike (a 4K job beside an image-track extraction), and a result under 1.0x returns as a brief against JS-141 and BL-234. Rejected: a literal 0.78 (refuses a play measured to hold), the 1.0x unit (drops the margin), repricing the table, evidence-only or restart-only recovery, an operator reset, no persistence, a per-pod key, a measurement task. Unverified when decided: that every price row carries the 1.2 margin; the 40 s convergence; whether a lowest-priority extraction still slows a 4K job; which way the figure moves during one. Reopens on: the spike showing one figure does not hold across rows by more than a fifth; failed timed rises logged on any deployment more than once a day; the dogfood, undeclared, with a heavy play under 1.0x within 5 minutes of a worker start (JS-178 moves to directly after JS-177); BL-262's trigger.
serves: PRODUCT.md goal 1: 'Playback never surprises a viewer.' 'A heavy film uses the whole cluster's processors rather than stalling on one machine while others sit idle.' 'Nothing breaks the viewers' evening. Upgrades, a lost machine and a database failover happen without interrupting anyone.' 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'. 'Installing is boring'. D-064: a worker learns what it holds; transcodeCores is an optional ceiling. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product.
